title: Kernel of a homogeneous quotient on a degree-one Proj chart
statement:
Let $S=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}S_d$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring (so $1\in S_0$ and $S_dS_e\subseteq S_{d+e}$), let $f\in S_1$, and let $K\subseteq S$ be a homogeneous ideal, meaning that every homogeneous component of every element of $K$ belongs to $K$. Give $C=S/K$ its quotient grading $C_d=\operatorname{im}(S_d\to C)$ and write $\bar f$ for the image of $f$. Use degree-zero homogeneous localizations [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero] with equality given by the ordinary localization relation [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. The quotient map induces a well-defined surjective ring homomorphism
$$q:S_{(f),0}\longrightarrow C_{(\bar f),0},\qquad s/f^d\longmapsto\bar s/\bar f^d\quad(s\in S_d).$$
Its kernel is the ideal $J$ of $S_{(f),0}$ generated by all fractions $s/f^d$ with $d\geq0$ and $s\in K\cap S_d$. Consequently it induces a canonical ring isomorphism $S_{(f),0}/J\cong C_{(\bar f),0}$ carrying the class of $s/f^d$ to $\bar s/\bar f^d$. These assertions allow $f$, $\bar f$ to be zero or nilpotent and allow $S$ or $C$ to be the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space, proof: description of J' as the ideal of fractions from I; the induced fraction map is Tag 01MY, lemma-morphism-proj, clause (2).

proof.text: Write $p:S\to C$ for the quotient map. The displayed images $C_d=p(S_d)$ form a direct grading: they span because every element of $S$ has a finite homogeneous decomposition. If $\sum_d p(s_d)=0$ with $s_d\in S_d$, then $\sum_ds_d\in K$; homogeneity of $K$ gives $s_d\in K$ separately, so every $p(s_d)=0$. Also $p(1)\in C_0$ and $C_dC_e\subseteq C_{d+e}$ by multiplying lifts. In particular $p(f)=\bar f\in C_1$ and every $c\in C_d$ has a lift in $S_d$.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space, proof: J' generated by homogeneous fractions; Tag 01MY, lemma-morphism-proj, clause (2) and its fraction formula.

proof.text: By [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], source and target chart elements have representatives $s/f^d$ and $c/\bar f^d$ of numerator degree $d$. Define $q(s/f^d)=p(s)/\bar f^d$. If $s/f^d=t/f^e$, [def-weil-ring-localization-away] gives $f^k(sf^e-tf^d)=0$ for some $k$. Applying $p$ gives $\bar f^k(p(s)\bar f^e-p(t)\bar f^d)=0$, hence equality of the proposed images. The addition and multiplication formulas in the same definition show that $q$ preserves sums and products: their numerators are respectively $sf^e+tf^d$ and $st$, both of degree $d+e$, and $p$ sends these to the corresponding target numerators. The representatives $0/1$ and $1/1$ show preservation of zero and one. Thus $q$ is the asserted well-defined ring homomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space, proof: J' generated by homogeneous fractions; Tag 01MY, lemma-morphism-proj, clause (2) and its fraction formula.

proof.text: For any target element, [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero] supplies a representative $c/\bar f^d$ with $c\in C_d$. By Step 1, choose $s\in S_d$ with $p(s)=c$. Then $q(s/f^d)=c/\bar f^d$. This proves surjectivity without any assumption that $\bar f$ is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space, proof: J' generated by homogeneous fractions; Tag 01MY, lemma-morphism-proj, clause (2) and its fraction formula.

proof.text: Every generator $s/f^d$ of $J$ has $p(s)=0$, so $q$ kills it and all finite sums of its multiples; hence $J\subseteq\ker q$. Conversely take $x=s/f^d\in\ker q$ using [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. Applying the equality relation of [def-weil-ring-localization-away] to $p(s)/\bar f^d=0/1$ gives $\bar f^np(s)=0$ for some $n\geq0$. Thus $f^ns\in K\cap S_{n+d}$. The defining localization relation also gives $s/f^d=(f^ns)/f^{n+d}$ (the cross-products are literally equal). The right side is one of the generators of $J$, so $x\in J$. Therefore $\ker q=J$.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space, proof: J' generated by homogeneous fractions; Tag 01MY, lemma-morphism-proj, clause (2) and its fraction formula.

proof.text: Put $A=S_{(f),0}$. Define $\widetilde q:A/J\to C_{(\bar f),0}$ by $[x]\mapsto q(x)$. If $[x]=[y]$, then $x-y\in J=\ker q$, so $q(x)=q(y)$; the map is well defined and preserves the ring operations by their quotient formulas. It is surjective by Step 3. If $\widetilde q([x])=\widetilde q([y])$, then $q(x-y)=0$, whence $x-y\in J$ by Step 4 and $[x]=[y]$. Its inverse sends a target element to the class of any preimage under $q$; this class is unique by the same calculation. The two maps are inverse ring homomorphisms, giving the canonical isomorphism and its stated formula. No step cancels $f$ or $\bar f$: for a nilpotent denominator the ordinary localization relation makes every fraction zero; if only $\bar f$ is nilpotent, Step 4 applied to $1/1$ gives $1\in J$. Thus the argument also includes all the zero-ring cases.
